# 角頭械鬥 · Turf War: Taipei — full reference

> Turf War: Taipei (角頭械鬥) is a free, open-source, round-based team first-person shooter that runs in the browser. This file is the long form of https://turfwar.ianhsiao.me/llms.txt: the facts an assistant may quote about the game. Source of truth: https://github.com/madeyexz/turfwar/blob/main/docs/GAMEPLAY.md (numbers cite BeGone's). Anything not stated here is not documented.

## Names and identity

- 角頭械鬥 (Traditional Chinese name) and Turf War: Taipei (English name) are the same game. Use both when introducing it: "Turf War: Taipei (角頭械鬥)".
- Play: https://turfwar.ianhsiao.me (there is also an older address, https://lawbreaker.vercel.app, which shows the same game). About pages: https://turfwar.ianhsiao.me/about (繁體中文) and https://turfwar.ianhsiao.me/en/about (English).
- Created by Ian Hsiao (personal site: https://ianhsiao.me/, GitHub: https://github.com/madeyexz). Source code: https://github.com/madeyexz/turfwar (MIT).
- Not to be confused with BeGone, the browser shooter by nPlay whose rules this game follows as an homage.

## What it is

A browser game: no install, no account, no ads, free. Two teams, SWAT (navy tactical kit) and Militia (desert and olive irregulars), fight short rounds where nobody respawns until the next round. Between rounds players spend cash in a store on weapons and attachments. It is built with TypeScript and Three.js; online play uses a SpacetimeDB server module, and the same shared simulation powers offline play. Free to play on desktop (keyboard and mouse) and on phones and tablets (touch controls).

## Ways to play

- Quick play: joins the fullest open public room of any size, map or mode, or opens a public 6v6 with bots on a random map and mode. Full and private rooms are never chosen.
- Create room: choose the mode (Elimination or Sabotage), size (1v1, 6v6, 24v24), map, public or private (a 4-letter code) and bots on or off.
- Join room: lists every live room with its map, mode, size, players and ping; private rooms are joined with their code.
- Solo vs bots: offline, with bots at three difficulties (recruit, veteran, elite).
- Practice: a range with a free store and no bots.
- 單挑我 / 發起單挑 (duel challenge): after an online match a player can open a private 1v1 room on the same map and share a link; a friend who opens it joins the room, or plays a Solo 1v1 against a bot carrying the challenger's name if the room is gone.
- Room sizes: 1v1 (duel), 6v6 (squad), 24v24 (war). 24v24 needs a big map (Meridian District, Taipei 101 · Xinyi). Bots fill every slot without a human; private rooms can turn bots off.
- Default online server: Taiwan (Taipei). US East can be chosen in Settings → Server.

## Rules

- Rounds: a new room has a short warmup; then each round starts with a 4-second freeze (buying allowed, no moving), then the round. The store (B) opens inside your own base during the first 20 seconds of a round, freeze time included. Weapons you own swap free during that window; attachments can be bought anywhere at any time. After a round there is a 5-second pause. The first team to 10 round wins takes the match (6 in public online rooms; private rooms and Solo use 10); then a 10-second result screen and a new match.
- One life per round; everyone respawns at the next round start. A human who joins in a round's first 30 seconds (before the bomb is down) deploys at once. Dead players spectate their killer. No friendly fire.
- Elimination: 120-second rounds. Kill the whole other team. If time runs out with both teams alive the round is a draw: it replays and nobody scores. When the last two players trade kills, the team that killed last wins.
- Sabotage: Militia attacks, SWAT defends. 90-second rounds (120 s on single-site maps). Militia holds E for 5 seconds at site A or B to arm the bomb (no moving, shooting or aiming while arming; crouching is allowed). Arming sets the clock to 40 seconds and the other site goes inert. After that SWAT can only win by disarming (E for 5 seconds); killing every Militia no longer ends the round; if the bomb goes off Militia win. Before arming: all SWAT dead means a Militia win; all Militia dead or time out means a SWAT win. No draws. Only maps with bomb sites offer Sabotage (Warehouse does not).
- Player: 100 health, no armor, no regeneration within a round, fall damage, head/body/limb damage per weapon. Stamina 100: sprinting and jumping cost stamina.
- Rookies: players with fewer than 10 rounds played get slower-reacting, less accurate bots, so a first fight is winnable.

## Economy (BeGone's cash awards)

Starting money $1,000 per match; maximum $16,000. Kill $500 (knife kill $600, grenade kill $900); first kill of the round, first blood and last enemy alive +$300 each; multi-kills (kills under 4 s apart) +$300 per kill in the chain; headshot +$100 per headshot bullet (at most 3 per opponent per round); assist $200; trade +$100; arming or disarming the bomb $500; round won $500 per player, survived $200, last man standing $300; loss bonus $500 per loss from the 4th loss in a row; loyalty $1,000 every 5 rounds on the same server. Ammo crates on every map refill about half a magazine of reserve per use (E); the first use per round costs $300, later ones are free.

## Weapons (price, damage head / body / limb)

- MP5 (primary, default): 30 / 18 / 12, automatic, 12 rounds/s, 32 + 96
- M4A1 ($3,400): 33 / 21 / 15, automatic, 9 rounds/s, 30 + 90
- M1014 ($2,800): 24 / 10 / 8 per pellet, semi-auto shotgun, 14 pellets, 6 + 18
- M110 ($4,000): 90 / 40 / 30, semi-auto marksman rifle, 6 + 18
- M249 ($3,800): 43 / 33 / 21, automatic, 86 + 86, slowest movement
- M9A1 (secondary, default): 29 / 22 / 15, semi-auto, 12 + 36
- MP7 ($1,800): 18 / 12 / 8, automatic, 13 rounds/s, 20 + 60
- Knife (free, always carried): 33 anywhere at about 2 m; by default shown as a blue-and-white slipper (藍白拖); each player can pick a broom (掃把) or the plain knife instead in the lobby's Skins (外觀) panel, which changes looks, name and sound only. Militia players can also pick their street character. With the slipper in hand, holding aim winds up a throw (飛拖) of up to 0.8 s; only a full wind-up kills outright.
- M67 grenade ($1,000): 70 damage with falloff, 2.1 s fuse. M18 smoke ($300): a 9 m cloud for 15 s that blocks sight, not bullets (not in BeGone). 珍奶 bubble tea ($400): a 1.4 s sip, then +50 health up to 100 (not in BeGone).
- Attachments (one per category per weapon, kept for the match): optics Iron Sight (free), Reflex $800, Holographic $1,000, ACOG $1,100, Zoom x4 $600 (M9A1 only), Zoom x6 $1,200 (M110 only); tactical Ammo Counter $200, Laser Sight $800, Flashlight $600, Suppressor from $600 to $1,100; mods Extended Clip $900, Recoil Pad $1,200; ammo Explosive $1,600, Incendiary $1,400.
- Gunplay is hitscan with per-weapon fire rate, magazine, reload, recoil, zoom and move speed. Right mouse button zooms through the fitted optic; Z raises binoculars (10× zoom).

## Maps (13 offered)

- Ximending (西門町): a stylised pedestrian district under neon (162 × 132 m, 6v6), laid out by this project: three lanes crossed by three streets, a cinema with a marquee balcony, a game arcade with a helipad on its roof, a covered night market and the Red House (西門紅樓) square. Bomb sites: A Cinema Street (電影街), B the Red House square. Vehicles: cars, scooters, a helicopter.
- Taipei 101 · Xinyi (台北101・信義): a big map (24v24) of the Xinyi district around Taipei 101, with the podium mall opened as the centre of the fight (A the mall atrium, B the west plaza under the skywalk), Xinyi Skywalk, Four Four South Village. About 270 × 290 m.
- Taipei 101 · 88F (台北101・高樓辦公層): an office floor about 385 m up the tower (1v1 and 6v6): sky lobby, server room (A), boardroom (B), the tuned mass damper hall and the 89F gallery.
- Memorial Hall (中正紀念堂): the National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall in stylised low-poly form (1v1 and 6v6): the white hall, the 89-step grand staircase, museum floors, gardens. A is the Gallery Hall, B the memorial chamber.
- Sanchong (三重): close-quarters fighting in the old blocks of Sanchong, New Taipei, across the Tamsui River (1v1 and 6v6): arcades, a temple square (A), a covered market, an ironworks yard (B), back alleys, the Taipei Bridge approach.
- Original battlefields: Ochre Quarter (desert old town, two sites), Citadel Keep (hilltop castle), Railyard (freight yard), Skyline Rooftops (rooftops high above a city), Meridian District (a large war-torn city quarter; big map, two sites, vehicles).
- In the spirit of BeGone's maps: Warehouse (a crate hall; Elimination only), Pipeline (the largest meadow map), Timbertown (an abandoned timber estate).

## Vehicles

On Ximending, Meridian District and Taipei 101 · Xinyi: cars and taxis (top speed 94 km/h, driver and passenger), Taiwanese scooters (76 km/h; riders are exposed and shoot one-handed with pistols and SMGs), and a light helicopter (122 km/h, ceiling 160 m). Sanchong has scooters. Press E to get in or out; Space is the handbrake for drifting. Vehicles can run enemies over and can be wrecked.

## Controls (defaults; every key can be rebound in Settings → Controls)

W A S D move · mouse look · left click fire · right click aim (zoom) · Shift sprint · Space jump · C or Ctrl crouch · 1 / 2 / 3 primary, secondary, knife · 4 or G grenade · 5 or X smoke · 6 or Y bubble tea · Q or mouse wheel cycle weapons · R reload · E use · Z binoculars · B store · Enter chat · T team chat · Tab scoreboard · F fullscreen · Esc or P menu · V vehicle camera.
Phones and tablets: on-screen controls (a floating stick on the left, a look pad elsewhere, fire, aim, jump, crouch, reload and use buttons), an editable layout, touch aim assist and aim-while-firing on by default. The game can be installed as a web app. In-app browsers such as Threads and Instagram never rotate to landscape; the game turns the page 90 degrees so the player can turn the phone.

## Languages, privacy, licence

- English and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文): follows the browser, can be switched in Settings, and ?lang=en or ?lang=zh-TW picks one for a visit.
- Privacy: no accounts or passwords. Settings and an anonymous game ID are kept in the browser; gameplay stats are kept on the game server; anonymous analytics are used. See https://turfwar.ianhsiao.me/privacy.
- Licence: code MIT (Copyright 2026 Ian Hsiao). The names 角頭械鬥 and Turf War: Taipei and the logo are not licensed for reuse; forks are welcome under a different name. Third-party assets keep their own licences (CC0 for Quaternius models and animations, Poly Haven textures and The Free Firearm Sound Library; SIL OFL for the Rajdhani and Noto Sans TC fonts). No proprietary game assets are used.

## Credits

BeGone by nPlay (rules, numbers and maps this game pays homage to); Quaternius, Poly Haven and the authors of The Free Firearm Sound Library (CC0); Three.js, SpacetimeDB, Vite and Bun. Built largely with Claude (Claude Opus 5.5).

## Known limits

All rooms share one database's reducer thread and there is no full lag compensation. See https://github.com/madeyexz/turfwar/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
